# Source: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md
design-rationale	prose: design rationale or recommended use; not a runtime invariant	If you reached for the typed door, say so: `sqlb.Fn` and the engine packages' escape hatches exist precisely so a missing helper never blocks you, and knowing you needed one tells us which helper to add.

# Source: AGENTS.md
contributor-policy	prose: instruction to contributors about review, releases or tooling	**Never suppress a diagnostic to make a gate pass.** No `//nolint`, no deleted assertion, no skipped test, no loosened type.
contributor-policy	prose: instruction to contributors about review, releases or tooling	**Never edit `pg` to add an extension.** Copy `pg/postgis`.
contributor-policy	prose: instruction to contributors about review, releases or tooling	A type-safety claim needs a line in `examples/typecheck/bad.go` that must not compile.
contributor-policy	prose: instruction to contributors about review, releases or tooling	`ci.yml` and `release.yml` are generated by `volt gen`; regenerate them, never edit them.
reviewer-policy	prose: instruction to documentation reviewers, not runtime behavior	Never cite a path and line.
reviewer-policy	prose: instruction to documentation reviewers, not runtime behavior	Never paste code.
reviewer-policy	prose: instruction to documentation reviewers, not runtime behavior	Never type a fact.
reviewer-policy	prose: instruction to documentation reviewers, not runtime behavior	Never ack a page wholesale.

# Source: CHANGELOG.md
external-extensions	test	Each has a README and a guard test, and each is built from the guarded constructors `pg` exports, so adding an extension never edits `pg`.
query-overlap	test	A Query holds pointers into the caller's variables, so sharing one across goroutines was a data race that interleaved rows silently; `One` and `Each` now refuse an overlapping execution instead.

contributor-policy	prose: instruction to contributors about review, releases or tooling	Never move or recreate a published tag: the Go checksum database has recorded it.
pg-live	test	Run the Postgres proof against the scratch Postgres 18 container, which is what covers the constructs 17 refuses - virtual generated columns, NOT ENFORCED constraints, the wider ALTER CONSTRAINT and temporal keys

# Source: COVERAGE.md
historical-context	prose: retrospective explanation of earlier defects or testing choices	The profile the go command writes for a multi-package run keeps one copy of each block instead of summing the copies, and the copy that survives is usually from a binary that never executed it.
typed-clauses	test	`examples/typecheck/bad.go` must never compile, so it is never executed and never counted.
design-rationale	prose: design rationale or recommended use; not a runtime invariant	A type-safety claim is proven by a compiler that refuses, not by a line that ran.

# Source: README.md
cross-package	test	It must let the application join across the boundary into tables it has never heard of, and it must do so without pulling a code generator or a second ORM into an application that may already have one.
external-extensions	test	- **Extensions are sub-packages over exported guarded constructors**, so adding pgvector support, or the next extension nobody has written yet, never edits the engine package.
engine-guard	test	The failure is still in your process and still names the construct — it is never a syntax error from the database at three in the morning.
pg-live	test	`sqlbtest` is a shared conformance suite every driver runs; `contrib/driver-sqlite` executes every `sqlite` construct against a real database, and `contrib/driver-pgx` executes every construct in `pg` and its eight extension packages — 593 cases — against Postgres 17, and the same suite again against Postgres 18 for the constructs 17 refuses.
cross-package	test	| A library can export typed columns for code that has never seen its schema | ✅ | ⚠️ only if both sides adopt the same tool | ❌ | ❌ |
cross-package	test	If you want a library's tables to be joinable by code that has never seen its schema, without either side adopting the other's ORM, that is `sqlb`.
connection-ownership	test	`sqlb` never opens a connection for you — it takes any `database/sql` handle, so `*sql.DB` and `*sql.Tx` both work and your existing pool is the pool.
query-overlap	test	`One` and `Each` refuse an overlapping execution with `ErrQueryInUse` rather than returning interleaved rows.
external-extensions	test	**A Postgres extension** is a sub-package built on the guarded constructors `pg` exports, so adding one never edits `pg`.
design-rationale	prose: design rationale or recommended use; not a runtime invariant	A missing helper is never a reason to go back to strings.
query-overlap	test	`One` and `Each` refuse an overlapping execution with `ErrQueryInUse` rather than returning corrupted results.

# Source: SECURITY.md
parameter-binding	test	In ordinary query mode, the security property it is responsible for is that a value which enters through `Param`, `Set`, `In` or a predicate leaves as a bound parameter and never as SQL text.

# Source: bind/README.md
stmt-boundary	test	**`Binding` is an interface owned by `stmt`, and must stay one.** The statement layer knows only that an item renders and carries an opaque target; it must never learn that the target is a pointer.

# Source: ch/README.md
coverage-limit	prose: explicit limit of the claimed verification scope	**This is not a ClickHouse client, and the README should not be read as claiming one.** It exists to prove the extension points carry a second engine, and it has never been executed against a server — say so rather than implying coverage.

# Source: contrib/debug/README.md
author-input-policy	prose: caller responsibility for author-supplied SQL, not input validation by the library	Renders a built statement with its arguments substituted, **for reading and never for running**.
parameter-binding	test	In ordinary query mode, `sqlb` never puts your values in the SQL.
parameter-binding	test	It emits markers and ships the values separately, which is why an injection cannot happen: a value containing `'; DROP TABLE users; --` is still a value, because it never travelled as SQL.
author-input-policy	prose: caller responsibility for author-supplied SQL, not input validation by the library	It is not guaranteed to be valid SQL for any particular engine, it does not attempt the escaping rules of every type a driver accepts, and it must never be sent to a database.

# Source: contrib/driver-pgx/README.md
pg-skip	test	Absence is a **loud skip**, never a silent pass: without the variable every test in this package skips with a message naming it, so a green gate with the proof skipped is visible in the skip count rather than mistaken for the proof having run.

# Source: contrib/driver-sqlite/README.md
migration-lock	test	A deferred transaction whose first statement reads holds a read lock, and SQLite refuses its upgrade to a write while another connection writes, without consulting the timeout; begin a transaction that will write with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on a pinned `*sql.Conn` instead.

# Source: contrib/driver-sqlite/docs/README.md
sqlite-pragmas	test	The next query may run on a different connection, where the pragma was never set, and nothing reports it.

# Source: contrib/driver-sqlite/docs/features.md
historical-context	prose: retrospective explanation of earlier defects or testing choices	One connection is the only setting where that cannot happen, and a test is never the place to debug it.
sqlite-pragmas	test	Anything the defaults get wrong for a caller is reachable by name, so a disagreement about one pragma never costs the other three.

# Source: contrib/migrate/README.md
schema-composition	test	A schema is only worth describing if something can act on the description without knowing who wrote it, and this package acts on a `Set` assembled from packages that never imported each other.
schema-order	test	The order is `schema.Set.Sorted` over the descriptions, so it is deterministic and cycle-checked.
schema-duplicate	test	A table two contributors both create is refused with `schema.ErrDuplicateTable`, naming both owners.
schema-missing	test	A foreign key to a table no contribution creates is refused with `schema.ErrMissingTable`, because `Install` is for a whole database installed together.
migration-pinning	test	`TestExecute_PinningIsWhatMakesAConnectionSettingHold` reproduces the failure an unpinned runner hits, deterministically: with one of two connections held busy, as a pool under load has, `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` runs on one connection and the next insert on the other, which still enforces the key and refuses the row.
migration-lock	test	While another connection holds SQLite's write lock the row's insert is refused as busy, and that is treated as the lock being held.
migration-lock	test	A deferred transaction whose first statement reads, a `SkipIf` guard say, holds a read lock, and SQLite refuses its upgrade to the write lock at once, without consulting `busy_timeout`, while another connection writes; so the ledger begins its SQLite transactions `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, taking the write lock up front where the busy timeout applies.
migration-ledger	test	A caller uses it to report a schema's version, or to refuse a database newer than its code without reading the ledger table's columns itself.
migration-ledger	test	After a rollback the ledger may hold `003_x` while the code knows only `001` and `002`; plain `Apply` skips what it recognises and says nothing, and the old code starts against a schema it was never written for.
migration-ledger	test	On all three engines the tests apply a history, apply it again to no effect, refuse an edited migration, and hold the lock on one connection while a second deploy starts: it waits, and once released finds the migration applied by the holder and applies nothing.
migration-ledger	test	They also show that on SQLite a failed migration leaves no ledger row, read `Applied` back before and after with every field, and that `RefuseUnknown` refuses the one unknown row by name, ignores an owner it was not given, and leaves plain `Apply` as it was.
historical-context	prose: retrospective explanation of earlier defects or testing choices	Before the fix each of the deterministic ones failed with `database is locked`, and the fresh-file run failed about one round in five.
migration-lock	test	The lock test is deterministic because a test where two deploys race only fails when their timing lines up, and the first version of this one passed with the lock removed.
schema-duplicate	test	That is worth a parameter: when two modules both declare `users`, the question is always which two, and a `Set` that did not record it could only report the name.
schema-order	test	The order is topological over foreign keys and **deterministic**: two runs over the same `Set` produce the same slice, so the output can be committed to a repository and diffed.
schema-boundary	test	`schema` describes and never does.

# Source: contrib/structbind/README.md
structbind-tag	test	A field with a `db:` tag uses that tag, always.
structbind-namer	test	The `Namer` is an argument to `New`, never a setting.
design-rationale	prose: design rationale or recommended use; not a runtime invariant	Such a list is a decision about somebody else's vocabulary that can never be complete, and it makes the output depend on whether a word happened to be in it.
structbind-empty	test	`ErrEmptyColumn` is only reachable through a custom `Namer`: every `Namer` in this package returns a non-empty name for a non-empty field, and a field name is never empty.
structbind-unchecked-type	test	And the Go type of a field is **never checked** against the column's: a field mapped to a differently typed database column builds without consulting the database.

# Source: contrib/vet/README.md
vet-schema-qualified	test	Tables are keyed by `CatalogueKey(schema, name)`: a table in the connection's default schema (`current_schema()`, `DATABASE()`, SQLite's `main`) is under its bare name and under `schema.name`, any other only qualified, so `auth.users` is compared with `auth.users` and never with a `users` in the default schema.
vet-key-columns	test	Keys are matched by their columns, never by name, because SQLite reports no foreign-key names and an unnamed key's name is the engine's; an unstated action is `NO ACTION`, which every engine reports for it.
vet-source-checks	test	The source checks always run; `--dsn` adds the schema diff.

# Source: ddl/README.md
ddl-authored	test	It is authored DDL, never derived: a builder renders what its author wrote, and when and in what order the statements run stays the application's decision.

# Source: dialect/README.md
capability-interfaces	test	**A dialect declines a capability by not implementing the interface, never by returning false**, so an engine is never made to lie about what it supports.

# Source: docs/bind/README.md
cross-package	test	A library exports a function returning its own `[]stmt.Binding` for a struct it owns; the application concatenates that with its own and never learns the library's column layout.
query-overlap	test	`One` and `Each` refuse an overlapping execution with `ErrQueryInUse`, but that is detection, not prevention — a struct-literal `Query` has no guard.
stmt-boundary	test	The statement layer has to put *something* in `Query.Targets`, but it must not know that the something is a pointer into a caller's variable.

# Source: docs/ch/README.md
design-rationale	prose: design rationale or recommended use; not a runtime invariant	`ch.ArgMax` is worth knowing about even if you never use ClickHouse: it answers "the id of the row with the highest cost" in one expression, which is a correlated subquery or a window function anywhere else.
typed-clauses	test	| `ch.SelectClause` | a clause for a SELECT on ClickHouse: an alias for the core's typed clause, so a statement of another dialect refuses it at compile time |

# Source: docs/conformance.md
historical-context	prose: retrospective explanation of earlier defects or testing choices	Their first run, on 2026-09-22, found three core constructs that rendered cleanly and failed on a real engine: `ESCAPE '\'` is an unterminated string in MySQL's default mode, a parenthesised set-operation branch is a syntax error in SQLite, and `concat()` with a bound value is refused by Postgres, which cannot type the parameter.
conformance-reset	test	Each case empties both tables first, so the order of the cases cannot matter and a failure is never inherited from the case before it.
zero-values	test	`Values` holds the zero value of a type with a `Build` or render method, which must fail with an error, never panic and never render.

# Source: docs/core-builder.md
parameter-binding	test	| `Param[T]` | a bound parameter; the value never reaches the SQL text |
author-input-policy	prose: caller responsibility for author-supplied SQL, not input validation by the library	| `Literal[T]` | a constant fragment, for `''` or `FALSE` as a fallback; never for request data |
query-overlap	test	`One` and `Each` refuse an overlapping execution with `ErrQueryInUse` rather than corrupting the result.
group-parentheses	test	Groups are always parenthesised, including a group of one.
design-rationale	prose: design rationale or recommended use; not a runtime invariant	The escape hatch exists so that a missing helper is never a reason to abandon the builder and go back to strings.

# Source: docs/cross-package.md
cross-package	test	The application will want the library's rows joined to tables the library has never heard of, and it will want that in one statement rather than three round trips stitched together in Go.
design-rationale	prose: design rationale or recommended use; not a runtime invariant	A library can export **SQL strings**, which gives the application no type safety and the library no control over what is done with them; it can export a **query API** for every join it can imagine, which is a combinatorial explosion it will never finish; or it can export **typed columns** and let the application compose them.
cross-package	test	`workspace` never learns that `authlite` exists.
cross-package	test	`authlite` never learns that any of the other three exist.

# Source: docs/ddl/README.md
ddl-authored	test	It is **authored** DDL, never derived.
section-heading	prose: heading or navigation, not an independent behavior claim	- [SQLite: keys, STRICT and what ADD COLUMN refuses](#sqlite-keys-strict-and-what-add-column-refuses)
section-heading	prose: heading or navigation, not an independent behavior claim	- [What Build refuses](#what-build-refuses)
ddl-column-validation	test	A column declared on another table is refused with `ErrForeignColumn`, and one defined twice with `ErrDuplicateColumn`.
ddl-json-default	test	It is checked with `json.Valid`, so invalid JSON fails `Build` with `ErrInvalidJSON` on every engine, and written as `('<json>')`, the one spelling all three accept: MySQL refuses a JSON column's plain literal default, measured.
mysql-backslash	test	MySQL still refuses a backslash in any literal, so a JSON default with an escaped character cannot be written for MySQL; bind it at insert instead.
ddl-empty-oneof	test	Inside a `CHECK` the column is written bare, since a table's own constraint cannot name it through an alias; an empty `OneOf` is refused with `ErrEmptyOneOf` rather than rendering `IN ()`.
ddl-column-validation	test	Each names its columns by value, never by string, and the statement checks at `Build` that the table defines every one: a key on a column it does not define fails with `ErrUnknownColumn`, and one on another table's column with `ErrForeignColumn`.
ddl-generated-default	test	A column with an identity cannot also have a default, which `Build` refuses with `ErrDefaultOnGenerated`.
ddl-generated-default	test	`NOT NULL` is not written on a generated column, because the application never writes it and the expression decides.
pg-ddl-live	test	All of it runs against Postgres 17 in `contrib/driver-pgx`, where the server enforces each clause: the identity refuses an explicit id, the deferred composite key raises `foreign_key_violation` when checked, and a second NULL collides under `NULLS NOT DISTINCT`.
ddl-table-validation	test	An engine action that belongs to one table says so by implementing `ddl.TableNamer`, and one that names columns by implementing `ddl.ColumnNamer`, and the statement refuses it on another table with `ErrForeignColumn`.
ddl-guarded-constraint	test	It accepts only a `pg.Guardable`: `CreateEnum`, and `AddConstraintStatement(c)`, which is `ADD CONSTRAINT` as a statement of its own on the table the constraint's `TableConstraint` names and refuses an unnamed constraint with `ErrUnnamedConstraint`, because an unnamed foreign key raises nothing on a second run and is added twice.
nontransactional-index	test	`Concurrently` builds without blocking writes, and Postgres refuses it inside a transaction, so its `Statement` has `Transactional` false and a runner must execute it alone.
pg-ddl-live	test	`WithCheckOption(pg.Local)` or `pg.Cascaded` refuses a write through the view that the view would not show.
pg-ddl-live	test	All of it runs on Postgres 17 in `contrib/driver-pgx`: the sequence's type and step are read back, the check option refuses a row, and the materialized view refreshes concurrently.
pg-function-quote	test	The body is the one place in this package a whole program is a string: the library author writes it, it is never built from input, and it is dollar-quoted with a tag it does not contain.
pg-trigger-params	test	`Params` lives on the `pg.Function` value since a function's argument types are part of the name every other statement identifies it by, and `CreateTriggerFunction` refuses a `Function` that declares any.
pg-ddl-live	test	Executed on Postgres 17: the trigger fires once over four updates, as its `WHEN` and `UPDATE OF` say, rows land in the partition their bound names, and a concurrent detach is refused inside a transaction.
section-heading	prose: heading or navigation, not an independent behavior claim	## SQLite: keys, STRICT and what ADD COLUMN refuses
sqlite-autoincrement	test	Use it only when rowids must never be reused.
section-heading	prose: section heading	**What ADD COLUMN refuses.** SQLite's `ADD COLUMN` cannot add every column `CREATE TABLE` can, and says so at runtime with an error about syntax.
sqlite-add-column	test	`Build` refuses the same things instead, naming the rule: `ddl.ErrAddNotNull` for a `NOT NULL` column with no literal default, `ErrAddNonConstantDefault` for an expression default, `ErrAddConstraint` for a key on the added column, and `sqlite.ErrAddStored` for a stored generated column.
historical-database-observation	prose: version-specific observation reported as history, not a cross-version guarantee	Three of those four SQLite refuses only when the table has rows; on an empty table it accepts them.
sqlite-add-column	test	`Build` refuses them unconditionally on purpose: the empty table is the test database and the table with rows is production, so accepting them is how a migration passes CI and fails on deploy.
sqlite-user-version	test	**PRAGMA.** `sqlite.SetUserVersion(n)` sets the integer SQLite keeps in the database header and never reads, a migration ledger with no table for a database one library owns.
sqlite-ddl-live	test	Executed on SQLite in `contrib/driver-sqlite`: the NOCASE unique index refuses a case variant, the query planner uses the partial index for a query with its filter, and the trigger writes one audit row over three updates.
sqlite-rebuild	test	`ErrRebuildIncomplete` and `ErrRebuildSameName` refuse a rebuild with nothing to copy or no new name.
section-heading	prose: heading or navigation, not an independent behavior claim	## What Build refuses
sqlite-time-default	test	SQLite has no time type, and the literal a `time.Time` would become matches no time the driver stores, so a default of one would never compare equal to a row the application wrote:
ddl-column-validation	test	A column made some other way than `Col` is refused with `ErrNotAColumn`, and an engine clause aimed at a position the statement does not render with `ErrUnknownPosition`.
sqlite-notnull-conflict	test	It is refused at `Build` rather than documented because of when the failure would otherwise arrive.
historical-context	prose: retrospective explanation of earlier defects or testing choices	SQLite accepts the definition, so the schema installs and every test that never writes a `NULL` to that column passes; the first `NULL` production writes fails with `NOT NULL constraint failed`, from a table whose declaration promised the opposite.
zero-values	test	A zero value is refused at `Build` with `ddl.ErrZeroValue` rather than rendering `PRIMARY KEY ()` or panicking: a key with no columns, a foreign key with no column pairs, a statement wrapping nothing, a `CreateTableReady{}` with no table.
nontransactional-index	test	`Transactional` is false for a statement Postgres refuses inside a transaction block, such as `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`; a runner must execute it on its own.
mysql-partitioning	test	MySQL's `Partitioning` uses it to require every primary and unique key to include the partition columns and to refuse any foreign key.
ddl-generated-default	test	A clause that belongs to one column, an identity or a collation, is made with `NewColumnClause`, which names the column as a `ColumnRef` (any column made by `Col` is one) and says which `ColumnPart` of the definition it fills: `PartAfterType` straight after the type, `PartConstraint` after the default, `PartValueSource` for a constraint that supplies the value and so refuses a default, `PartComputed` for a generated expression, which also writes no `NOT NULL`, and `PartAfterNotNull` immediately after the `NOT NULL` and before the default.
ddl-extra-columns	test	The statement hands each column its rendered clauses as a `ColumnExtras`, whose `AfterType`, `Constraints`, `ValueSource`, `Computed`, `AfterNotNull` and `RequiresDefault` fields say what to write and what to refuse, so a `ColumnSpec` written outside this package can honour them.
historical-context	prose: retrospective explanation of earlier defects or testing choices	Before this, a caller who passed two correct clauses in the wrong order got a clean `Build` and then a server error about SQL they never wrote.
section-heading	prose: heading or navigation, not an independent behavior claim	### Why sort, rather than refuse or leave it
section-heading	prose: section heading	- **Refuse.** Fail `Build` when the order is wrong.
ddl-ordering	test	The statement reorders only what it understands, which is the one rule that never turns a correct statement into a wrong one.
ddl-describe	test	A column `Build` cannot spell fails `Describe` too, so a description never exists for DDL that does not.
pg18-live	test	Postgres 17 refuses the statement, so the execution tests run them against a scratch 18 (`task engines:pg18:up` then `task test:pg18`) and skip loudly elsewhere.
pg18-live	test	`pg.GeneratedVirtual(col, e)` is a generated column evaluated when it is read rather than stored, which is 18's default for `GENERATED ALWAYS AS`.
pg18-live	test	Enforcing it afterwards is `pg.AlterConstraint(c).Enforced()`, and that is for a foreign key: Postgres 18 refuses to change a check's enforceability, measured, so a check is turned on by dropping it and adding it enforced.

# Source: docs/ddl/not-built.md
literal-refusal	test	Quote identifiers with the dialect's `QuoteIdent`, and write a value with its `QuoteLiteral`, which refuses what it cannot write faithfully rather than guessing.
nontransactional-index	test	Set `Transactional: false` only for a statement Postgres refuses in a transaction block, such as `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`.
ddl-standalone	test	`ddl.NewStandaloneAlterClause[D]` is the same except that the action always gets a statement of its own.
ddl-inline	test	A DDL statement never takes bound values, because no engine accepts a placeholder in DDL.
coverage-limit	prose: explicit limit of the claimed verification scope	Each one is either refused at `Build` or documented where it is used.

sqlite-ddl-live	test	Measured on 3.50.3, this is what each action does to a row that leaves the column null: `OrReplace` writes the column's **`DEFAULT`** and keeps the row — the reason to reach for the clause at all — `OrIgnore` skips the whole row and reports success, and `OrAbort`, `OrFail` and `OrRollback` all refuse it as the plain `NOT NULL` does, differing only in how much they undo.

sqlite-notnull-conflict	test	It is refused rather than documented because of when the failure would otherwise arrive: SQLite accepts the definition, so the table installs and every test that never writes a `NULL` there passes, and the first `NULL` production writes fails with `NOT NULL constraint failed`.
sqlite-notnull-conflict	test	The other four actions never write the default, so they build without one.
sqlite-raise	test	`RaiseRollback` undoes the whole transaction, `RaiseAbort` undoes only the statement (SQLite's own default for a constraint violation), and `RaiseFail` stops the statement where it is and **keeps the changes it has already made**, which is almost never what a validation wants.
author-input-policy	prose: caller responsibility for author-supplied SQL, not input validation by the library	They are authored text like every other value in `ddl` — never a value that arrived in a request, which is the one thing that cannot be made safe in that position.

sqlite-page-size	test	`sqlite.SetPageSize` refuses that value instead.

query-overlap	test	`Query` also carries an execution guard, reachable as `Acquire` and `Release`, which [`exec`](../exec/README.md) uses to refuse an overlapping execution.

# Source: examples/cookbook/README.md
cross-package	test	The application wants the library's rows joined to tables the library has never heard of, in one statement; the library cannot write that join, and the application cannot either unless the library hands over something to join *on*.
cross-package	test	`workspace` never learns that `authlite` exists.
cross-package	test	`authlite` never learns that any of the other three exist.

# Source: examples/cookbook/authlite/README.md
cross-package	test	- **Query methods** that accept `sqlb.Option`, so the application can add a join, a filter or a column the library has never heard of.
connection-ownership	test	The caller owns the transaction; the library never begins one.

# Source: examples/typecheck/README.md
typed-clauses	test	The one file in this repository that **must not compile**.
typed-clauses	test	If a line ever starts compiling, either the construct got looser or the promise was never true — both are findings, and the gate is what turns them into a failed build instead of a surprise.

# Source: exec/README.md
query-overlap	test	`One` and `Each` refuse an overlapping execution with `ErrQueryInUse`; the guard is inherited by every statement derived from the builder.

# Source: pg/README.md
external-extensions	test	**Extensions never edit this package** — that is what the exported guarded constructors are for.

# Source: scan/README.md
scan-concurrency	test	**Nothing here takes the query guard, and adding one would be a regression.** A `Reader` holds no caller memory, so the guard would refuse a concurrent execution that is safe, contradicting the one property this package exists to offer.

# Source: schema/README.md
schema-order	test	Table descriptions, the per-engine type spelling table, and a deterministic topological sort, so two packages that own tables can be migrated together.
schema-boundary	test	**It describes and never does.** No DDL, no connection, no migration; those live above it, and `contrib/migrate` is the consumer that proves it carries its weight by executing its generated plan against a real database.

# Source: stmt/README.md
builder-immutability	test	**A builder method returns a derived statement and never writes to its receiver.** `base.Where(x)` leaves `base` alone, so deriving several queries from one template is safe by construction rather than by remembering `Clone`.

# Source: docs/dialects.md
render-errors	test	It also carries the first error. `Unsupported` records a construct the dialect cannot render, `Fail` records anything else, and `Build` returns whichever came first. Built-in validation returns an error rather than a partial query. This is not a panic recovery boundary: caller-supplied dialects and render callbacks remain responsible for their own behavior.

pg-websearch	test	| `pg.WebsearchToTSQuery` | WebsearchToTSQuery accepts malformed search-query text without a query-syntax error |
pg-json-wrapper	test	| `pg.WithWrapper` | WithWrapper wraps a matched result in an array |
